From the identity $1-{cos}^{2}⁡\theta ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =x+\frac{\pi }{4},$ we get 

$$
1-{cos}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4})={sin}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4}).
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{1-{cos}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4})}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}\frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4})}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}{csc}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{4})\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{4})-[-\operatorname{cot}⁡(0+\frac{\pi }{4})] \\  & =-\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =-0+1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
